findings.title: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without a lock while BuildIndex now writes to it concurrently
findings.body: `TotalDocs` ranges over `b.cache` without taking `cacheMu`. `searchSupport.init` now calls it in the new "search index initialized" log line, right after it starts the watch goroutine. That goroutine's `handleEvent` calls `getOrCreateIndex`, which can call `BuildIndex` and write `b.cache[key] = idx` under the lock. The PR also narrows the lock to cover only that write, so builds from many goroutines now hit the map at the same time. Iterating a Go map while another goroutine writes it can cause a fatal 'concurrent map iteration and map write' crash. `TotalDocs` should take `cacheMu.RLock()`.

findings.title: Removing the BuildIndex lock allows duplicate concurrent builds of the same index
findings.body: `BuildIndex` no longer holds `cacheMu` while building, and it never checks the cache for an existing entry before creating the index. `getOrCreateIndex` is a check-then-build with no per-key guard, so two callers can both see a miss for the same key. Examples are startup `init` racing with a Search request, or a watch event arriving during startup. Both then run `BuildIndex`. For file-backed indexes the second `bleve.New(dir, ...)` fails because the directory already exists, or both write the same directory. For memory indexes the second build overwrites the cache entry and leaks the first index, and the `IndexTenants` and `IndexedKinds` metrics are double counted. The coarse lock hid the concurrency but did not remove this problem. A per-key single-flight or an existence check under the lock is needed.

findings.title: Failed eager Init leaks the server's context and goroutines
findings.body: `NewResourceServer` now runs `s.Init(ctx)` synchronously, including the full index build. On failure it returns `nil, err` without calling `s.cancel()` or `lifecycle.Stop`. If `search.init` or `initWatcher` already started pollers or goroutines from `WatchWriteEvents` before failing, they keep running. The backend lifecycle is also never stopped. The cancelable context created just above is leaked. Cancel the context and stop the lifecycle on the error path.

findings.title: Eager Init makes construction block for the whole index build and fail hard
findings.body: Index building previously happened lazily on the first gRPC call. It now blocks `NewResourceServer`, so the process cannot serve health checks or `/metrics` until every index is built. Any build error also makes server construction fail rather than surfacing as a per-request error. The PR description itself asks what depends on lazy init, but nothing in the PR shows that this was examined. Callers such as the module server and tests that build the resource server during wire-up are affected, and the Postgres test had to be skipped in the same PR.

findings.title: Test skipped for postgres rather than fixed
findings.body: The test is skipped on Postgres with a TODO because it does not work in Drone. This is the same PR that moves initialization to server construction, so the failure may be caused by the change, for example init failing or taking too long at startup. Skipping removes the only coverage for the storage-server module target on that database and hides any regression.

findings.title: Trace context fix is incomplete; other backend spans still discard ctx
findings.body: The PR is meant to fix trace propagation, but only `GetResourceStats` was changed to `ctx, span :=`. `WriteEvent`, `ReadResource` and `ListIterator` in this file still use `_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)`. `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` has the same pattern. Their child spans (create, update, delete and the DB calls) therefore are not nested under these spans and stay detached from the parent trace.
